content:
Phase 70 implemented per the approved plan (docs/phases/standing-orders.md @ fd4fda3). Branch phase-70-standing-orders. gate: see entry.

What changed, where:
- tagteam/orders.py (new): load_project (safe_read, never raises; malformed/symlink → no orders + warn), run_override, effective() (run > run-mode > project > default), decide() (fresh impl APPROVE only; None without explicit orders; convert queue = [approved] + topological_queue, exhausted → complete, any roadmap failure → stop/roadmap-invalid), apply_decision()/keep_run_override() (the recorded decision only; convert materialised and override dropped only on the fresh write), render_block (capped), state_line, and the `tagteam orders` CLI.
- tagteam/cycle.py: add_round records run_decision on a fresh impl APPROVE (also via add_ruling) and passes fresh_decision=True; _derive_top_level_state applies the recorded decision and preserves `orders`; stderr note on a recorded decision; `cycle rounds` prints the block to stderr; tagteam-orders.json added to _TAGTEAM_ARTIFACT_FILES.
- tagteam/watcher.py: the roadmap-complete write uses clear_keys=["orders"] (the only watcher edit).
- tagteam/headless.py: compose_prompt(orders_block=…), after the interjections block.
- tagteam/state.py: an `Orders:` line, only with explicit orders.
- tagteam/cli.py: dispatch, help, READ_ONLY_COMMANDS allows the bare/--json read only.
- Contract (data + plugin copy, hash recorded) and workflows.md (data + docs copy).

One deviation from the plan text, deliberately: run-override writes use write_state under the writer lock WITHOUT bumping seq. A seq bump reads as a new turn to the watcher (tick() dispatches on a new seq), so `orders --run` during an owed turn would re-dispatch it. Pinned by test_run_write_does_not_bump_seq. Also added (not in the plan): a one-line stderr note for every recorded decision, not only for roadmap-invalid.

Verification: tests/test_orders.py has 51 tests covering criteria 1–13 (precedence table, no-orders byte-identity for single-phase and full-roadmap, convert → the unchanged _try_roadmap_advance starts the next ready phase and respects a dependency, already-Complete / ad-hoc phase as queue head, exhausted, three invalid-roadmap shapes, --run stop phase halting a roadmap run, continue keeping completed [A] → C starts with [A,B], override lifetime across REQUEST_CHANGES/NEED_HUMAN/ESCALATE/rulings, roadmap-complete and blocked pause, sync idempotency (a)(b)(c), delivery, CLI, read-only, symlink/malformed refusal, scope). I mutation-checked the three cycle.py hooks (no preservation / no apply / fresh always True); each is caught. I smoke-tested the real CLI in a scratch git project: orders stop/add, cycle rounds stderr block, the approve note, the `tagteam state` Orders line, and the read-only refusal (exit 2). Not exercised: a live watcher process dispatching after a convert. The tests call the unchanged _try_roadmap_advance directly instead.

Gate bounce fixed at 7ad6b4e. test_every_cli_command_is_documented wanted `tagteam orders` in README / docs/how-tagteam-works.md. It is now in both command blocks, with an `orders` bullet in the arbiter-controls notes. No code changed since r1. gate: see entry.

The r1 submission still stands for everything else. Summary: tagteam/orders.py (new) plus hooks in cycle.py (decide at the fresh impl APPROVE, apply the recorded run_decision, preserve `orders`), watcher.py (roadmap-complete drops the override), headless.py (prompt block), state.py (Orders line) and cli.py. Contract, workflows, README and HTW docs updated. tests/test_orders.py has 51 tests covering criteria 1–13, and the cycle.py hooks were mutation-checked.

Deviations from the plan text:
(1) Run-override writes don't bump seq, because a seq bump would re-dispatch the owed turn in the watcher. Pinned by a test.
(2) Every recorded decision prints a one-line stderr note, not only roadmap-invalid.

The r1 gate run: 2,345 passed, 5 skipped, 1 failed (this docs test).

GATE: PASS | scope 14 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2346 passed, 5 skipped, 7m55s)
checked: HEAD 7ad6b4e

Reviewed implementation at 7ad6b4e against the approved plan. The gate reports 2346 passed, 5 skipped at this HEAD; I did not rerun the full suite. Focused verification: tests/test_orders.py passed (51 tests, 5.45s). Additional isolated temporary-project checks reproduced the first two findings below. No advisory orders or interjections were present for this review.

1. [P1] A repeated APPROVE re-decides and can reverse a recorded stop (tagteam/cycle.py:593-600). The state checked here was already overwritten by _TRANSITIONS[action] at line 559, so state == approved does not establish a fresh approval. add_round accepts another APPROVE on the already-approved cycle, deletes its run_decision, and resolves against the state after the first approval cleared the run override. Reproduced with project stop=roadmap, run stop=phase, and a valid two-phase roadmap: first APPROVE leaves single-phase; repeating the same round's APPROVE changes it to full-roadmap. A retry can therefore restart a run that the arbiter explicitly stopped. Detect the actual transition using the pre-write cycle state under the writer lock; reject duplicate approval or preserve/reapply its recorded decision without marking it fresh. Cover a duplicate stop approval, and an override queued for the next run surviving a repeated approval of the old cycle.

2. [P2] The CLI can successfully write orders its own reader refuses (tagteam/orders.py:310-320). load_project caps input at MAX_BYTES=65536, but _write_project never checks the serialized byte length. Reproduced by setting project stop=roadmap and adding one 65536-character note: the command returns 0, writes 65719 bytes, then effective() reports explicit=False / stop=phase / over size limit. All prior notes and the enforced order disappear from delivery/enforcement, and subsequent remove/unset commands refuse the file. Validate the final encoded payload against MAX_BYTES before creating/replacing anything; reject the write with a useful error and leave the original file intact. Test cumulative notes and escaped/non-ASCII text at the boundary, not just a single note's character count.

3. [P2] The planned doctor warning is absent. The approved plan's storage section explicitly requires unreadable/malformed orders to produce a warning in both orders and doctor. tagteam/diagnostics.py:551-570 never reads orders or adds a finding, and no doctor test was added. Since dispatch intentionally falls back to no project orders, doctor needs to expose that fallback. Reuse the guarded reader and add read-only diagnostics tests for malformed, oversized and symlinked orders, while keeping a missing file quiet and avoiding note-content disclosure.

The continue/convert distinction and preservation of roadmap.completed are implemented as planned. The no-seq-bump deviation is reasonable for avoiding duplicate watcher dispatch; the findings above still need correction before approval.

All three r2 findings fixed at c8e5640. gate: see entry.

1. [P1] Repeated APPROVE (tagteam/cycle.py add_round). It now captures `prior_cycle_state` from the status file before the transition, under the writer lock. A decision is made only on a real transition into approved (prior != approved). A repeated APPROVE of an approved cycle keeps its recorded run_decision (no pop) and derives with fresh_decision=False: the recorded decision is re-applied, never re-decided, and no override is consumed. I kept "preserve and re-apply" rather than rejecting duplicates, so existing callers that re-approve still work. Tests: test_repeated_approve_does_not_redecide_a_stopped_run (your scenario: project roadmap, run phase; the second APPROVE leaves the decision and single-phase unchanged) and test_repeated_approve_keeps_an_override_queued_for_the_next_run. Both fail with the fix removed.

2. [P2] Write size (orders._write_project). The final encoded payload is checked against MAX_BYTES before the temp file is created. The refusal says the size and the limit, and says the file is unchanged. Test: one 64 KB note is refused with the file byte-identical, then escaped non-ASCII notes ("é" * 1500, about 9 KB each after json.dumps) are added until one is refused. The last accepted file is still under the limit and still read (stop and notes intact), with no temp file left behind. Fails with the check removed.

3. [P2] Doctor. orders.doctor_view() uses the same guarded reader. An absent file gives None (quiet). A valid file gives `ok` with the stop order and the note count, never note text. Malformed, oversized or symlinked gives `warn` "… — the engine treats this as no project orders" and counts in doctor's warn total. Report.orders (JSON) plus a "Standing orders" section in text. Tests in tests/test_diagnostics.py::TestStandingOrders: missing is quiet; valid doesn't disclose a note's text; the three bad shapes are warns in text and JSON. The doctor section of workflows.md mentions it.

Focused runs: test_orders + test_diagnostics 113 passed; test_plugin + test_framework + test_docs_story 169 passed.

GATE: PASS | scope 16 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2354 passed, 5 skipped, 8m05s)
checked: HEAD c8e5640

Approved implementation at c8e5640. All r2 findings are resolved: repeated approval checks the prior cycle state under the writer lock and preserves the recorded decision and any next-run override; project writes reject an oversized encoded payload before creating a temp file or replacing existing orders; doctor uses the guarded reader and reports invalid orders without disclosing advisory text. Regression tests cover the reported cases, including cumulative escaped non-ASCII notes.

Verification: accepted the gate's 2354 passed, 5 skipped at c8e5640; no full-suite rerun. Independently ran tests/test_orders.py and tests/test_diagnostics.py: 113 passed in 5.95s. Reviewed the changes since 7ad6b4e and their integration with the previously reviewed implementation. No remaining blocking findings. No standing advisory orders or interjections applied to this turn.
